material: black phosphorus, bulk (39 nm free-standing exfoliated film)
experiment_citation: H. Seiler et al., Accessing the anisotropic nonthermal phonon populations in black phosphorus, Nano Lett. 21, 6171 (2021), doi:10.1021/acs.nanolett.1c01786
D. Zahn et al., Anisotropic nonequilibrium lattice dynamics of black phosphorus, Nano Lett. 20, 3728 (2020), doi:10.1021/acs.nanolett.0c00734

conditions.electron_beam: along b (out of plane); probed plane (h0l)

pipeline.phonons: MACE medium-omat-0 force constants (fc2, fc3), full-grid three-phonon kernel
pipeline.electron_phonon: universal sp3 Slater-Koster tight binding (Harrison 1980), scissor to 0.33 eV

electrons.model: universal sp3 Slater-Koster (Harrison 1980) + NIST LDA term values

definitions.delta_MSD: change of the atom-averaged mean-square displacement projected on the Bragg vector G, Delta U_G(t) = G^.Delta U(t).G^ (A^2), equal to -ln(I/I0)/|G|^2 for black phosphorus (one Wyckoff site); zigzag = (h00), armchair = (00l)
definitions.biexp: Delta(t) = A1 (1 - exp(-t/tau1)) + A2 (1 - exp(-t/tau2)) for t > 0, convolved with a 150 fs FWHM Gaussian; tau1 < tau2; the simulated curve (50 fs pump) is first convolved with the 141 fs probe so that the total response is 150 fs
definitions.diffuse: one-phonon intensity at Q = q + G in the (h0l) plane, in the zone around (400), at the symmetry-equivalent points closest to (400); dI/I0 = I(t)/I(t<0) - 1 (time constants are the same for Delta I = I(t) - I(t<0)); single exponential: A (1 - exp(-t/tau)); biexponential as above (a rise and a slower relaxation appear as one positive and one negative amplitude); rise x decay: A (1 - exp(-t/tau_r)) exp(-t/tau_d) + C (1 - exp(-t/tau_d)); all convolved with 150 fs
definitions.points: Setyawan-Curtarolo labels of the base-centred orthorhombic zone, relative to (400): X = (4 +- 0.55, 0, 0), Z = (4, 0, +-0.5), A = (4 +- 0.55, 0, +-0.5), Y = (4 +- 1, 0, 0), T = (4 +- 1, 0, +-0.5) in conventional reciprocal-lattice units; X uses the nearest q-grid point (0.5 a* from the Bragg peak); the labels X1 and A1 are equivalent to X and A (identical traces); Y and T sit on glide-forbidden positions (h odd) of the (h0l) plane

characteristic_times.lattice_equilibration_definition: time after which the spread of branch effective temperatures falls below 10% of its maximum

sensitivity.note: the universal tight-binding coupling is uncertain by about a factor of 2 in |g|^2; these runs bracket the central prediction

expected_accuracy: Phonon frequencies and anharmonicity from the MACE foundation model: frequencies within ~5 %, three-phonon rates within a factor ~1.5-2 (graphite: lifetimes 2x shorter than DFT). Electron-phonon coupling from Harrison's universal hoppings: within a factor ~2 in |g|^2; the tight-binding bands of black phosphorus have a 3.8 eV gap before the scissor, so the band curvature near the edges, and hence the carrier phase space, is the least reliable input. Absorbed energy: from the stated optical constant (+-15 %). No recombination: the gap energy (0.33/1.61 = 20 % of the absorbed energy) stays in the carriers, so late-time Debye-Waller amplitudes are a lower bound if carriers recombine within 100 ps. Time constants are expected within a factor ~2, amplitudes within ~30 %.
